_meta.description: High-resolution micro-step funnels for business scenarios

saas_builder.name: SaaS Builder
saas_builder.description: Build a SaaS product from idea to $1M ARR — the full indie/startup path with real survival rates at each stage
saas_builder.entry_point: Person identifies a recurring problem they or others face and considers building software to solve it

stages.label: Notice a problem that could be solved with software
Identify a real, recurring problem worth solving
Talk to 10+ potential users and confirm they have the problem
Commit to actually building (not just researching)
Choose tech stack and architecture
Start building MVP — first lines of code
Survive 30 days of building without quitting
Complete MVP (functional, deployable product)
Launch publicly (Product Hunt, HN, Twitter, Reddit)
Get first 10 free signups from strangers
Collect feedback and iterate on MVP based on real usage
Convert one person to a paying customer
Reach $100 MRR
Identify and fix early churn (5-7% monthly is typical)
Reach $1K MRR
Find one repeatable growth channel (SEO, content, paid, referral)
stages.source: First Round Capital State of Startups 2024

stages.label: Reach $5K MRR
Make first hire (contractor or part-time)
Reach $10K MRR
Push through the $10K-$30K MRR plateau
Reach $50K MRR
Reach $1M ARR ($83K MRR)

saas_builder.end_to_end_conversion: 0.7% — of 1,000 people who identify a SaaS idea, roughly 7 reach $1M ARR within 5 years. Median time to $1M ARR is 5 years (ChartMogul 2025). Only 13.4% of launched SaaS products reach $1M ARR in 3 years.
sources: First Round Capital State of Startups 2024

local_business.name: Local Business (Restaurant/Shop/Cafe)
local_business.description: Open a physical local business from dream to multi-location — restaurants, cafes, shops, salons with real BLS survival data
local_business.entry_point: Person dreams of opening their own restaurant, cafe, or retail shop and begins exploring the idea seriously

stages.label: Want to own a business
Dream about opening a business (talk about it, Pinterest boards, etc.)
Research the local market, competitors, foot traffic, demographics
Create a written business plan with financial projections
Secure funding (savings, loan, investors, family) — avg $50K-$250K
Find a suitable location (foot traffic, rent, size, zoning)
Sign lease agreement (avg 3-5 year commitment)
Renovate, design, equip the space
Obtain all required permits, licenses, health inspections
Hire and train initial staff
Soft opening — friends, family, test runs
Grand opening day — doors open to public
Survive month 1 — cash flow crunch, operational chaos
Build a base of regular/repeat customers
Survive year 1 (83% of all businesses do)
Reach monthly breakeven (revenue covers all costs)
Survive year 3 (65% of all businesses do)
Become consistently profitable (net positive after owner salary)
Survive year 5 (51% of all businesses do)
Systemize operations (SOPs, management layer, not owner-dependent)
Open second location or franchise

local_business.end_to_end_conversion: 2.1% — of 1,000 people who dream of opening a local business, roughly 21 end up with a profitable, systemized business at year 5. For restaurants specifically, 60% fail in year 1 (National Restaurant Association), making food service the hardest vertical.

partnership_business.name: Partnership Business (Start with a Friend/Co-founder)
partnership_business.description: Start a business with a partner — from exciting idea to either scaling together or painful breakup, with Harvard data on co-founder conflict
partnership_business.entry_point: Two friends or colleagues have a business idea together and get excited about building it

stages.label: Have a friend/acquaintance with shared interest
Have a business idea with a friend — mutual excitement
Sit down and discuss it seriously (not just bar talk)
Agree on who does what (roles and responsibilities)
Agree on equity split (50/50 is most common and most dangerous)
Actually formalize with LLC/contract/operating agreement
stages.source: Wasserman — 80% of partnerships lack written agreements

stages.label: Both invest first money (savings, equipment, time off work)
Build together for first month — honeymoon phase
Continue building for 3 months — reality sets in
First real disagreement (strategy, effort, direction, money)
Successfully resolve the disagreement without resentment
Launch product or service together
Generate first revenue together
Have the hard money conversation (who gets paid what, reinvest vs distribute)
Partnership survives year 1 together
Navigate effort imbalance (one partner working more than the other)
Major conflict point (pivot, money, new partner, exit, life changes)
stages.source: Wasserman — 65% fail due to co-founder conflict

stages.label: Both partners choose to continue (no exit)
Restructure roles and equity based on actual contribution
Scale the business together past $500K revenue
Partnership intact and thriving at year 3

partnership_business.end_to_end_conversion: 1.8% — of 1,000 pairs who get excited about a business idea together, roughly 18 end up with a thriving partnership at year 3. 65% of startups fail due to co-founder conflict (Wasserman, Harvard). The #1 killer is unequal effort + 50/50 equity.
sources: Noam Wasserman — The Founder's Dilemmas (Harvard Business School) 2012
First Round Capital State of Startups Review 2024

affiliate_marketing.name: Affiliate Marketing (Blog/SEO/Content)
affiliate_marketing.description: Build an affiliate marketing business through content and SEO — from picking a niche to earning $10K/month, with brutal conversion reality
affiliate_marketing.entry_point: Person learns about affiliate marketing (YouTube, course, blog post) and decides to try it as a side income

stages.label: Discover affiliate marketing exists
Learn about affiliate marketing (watch videos, read guides)
Pick a niche (often too broad or too competitive first time)
Buy domain and hosting, set up WordPress/blog
Write and publish first 10 articles
Learn SEO fundamentals (keyword research, on-page, link building)
Reach 30 published articles with keyword targeting
Reach 50 published articles (the content threshold)
Wait for Google indexing and ranking (the sandbox period)
stages.source: Ahrefs Study: 95% of pages get zero Google traffic in first year 2024

stages.label: Get first consistent organic traffic (100+ visits/month)
stages.source: Ahrefs — 5.7% of pages rank in top 10 within 1 year 2024

stages.label: Apply to affiliate programs (Amazon, ShareASale, niche programs)
Get accepted to relevant affiliate programs
Get first affiliate link clicks from organic traffic
Make first affiliate sale
Reach $100/month in affiliate commissions
Reach $500/month
Diversify across multiple affiliate programs and networks
Reach $1,000/month (top 5% of affiliates)
Build email list (1,000+ subscribers) for direct monetization
Reach $5,000/month
Reach $10,000/month (top 1% of affiliates)
stages.source: Authority Hacker — top 10% earn 90% of all affiliate income 2024

affiliate_marketing.end_to_end_conversion: 0.3% — of 1,000 people who start learning affiliate marketing, roughly 3 reach $10K/month. 95% of affiliates earn less than $1K/month. The top 10% earn 90% of all affiliate income. Average time to first sale: 6-12 months. 95% of new pages get zero Google traffic in the first year.
sources: Authority Hacker Annual Affiliate Marketing Survey 2024

newsletter_media.name: Newsletter/Media Business
newsletter_media.description: Build a newsletter or media business from scratch to $10K/month — through consistent publishing, audience building, and monetization
newsletter_media.entry_point: Person decides to start a newsletter on a topic they know or care about, often inspired by successful newsletter creators

stages.label: Have knowledge/interest in a topic
Choose a topic/niche for the newsletter
Set up on Substack, Beehiiv, ConvertKit, or Ghost
Write and publish first issue
Share with friends, social media, existing network
Publish consistently for 1 month (4 issues)
stages.source: Substack — 90% of newsletters go inactive within 6 months 2024

stages.label: Reach 100 subscribers
Maintain weekly publishing for 3 months (12+ issues)
Find your unique voice/angle that differentiates from others
Reach 500 subscribers
Reach 1,000 subscribers (top 10% of newsletters)
Implement growth tactics (cross-promos, referral programs, SEO)
Receive first sponsorship inquiry
stages.source: Sponsorship rates start at 1K-2K subs (Newsletter Operator 2024)

stages.label: Close first paid sponsorship deal ($25-$50 CPM)
Reach 5,000 subscribers
Reach $500/month revenue (sponsorships + affiliates)
Reach 10,000 subscribers
Launch paid subscription tier ($5-$15/month)
Reach $2,000/month (paid subs + sponsors)
Reach 50,000 subscribers
Reach $10,000/month revenue

newsletter_media.end_to_end_conversion: 0.5% — of 1,000 people who start a newsletter, roughly 5 reach $10K/month. 90% of newsletters go inactive within 6 months. 90% never reach 1,000 subscribers. Average open rate is 43% but click rate only 2%. The newsletter business is a consistency game — most people quit before the compounding kicks in.
